headline: Margins normalize as inventory gains unwind;

highlights: Volumes recovered to 619k MT (+4.21% QoQ / -8.02% YoY) as deliveries to Middle East smelters resumed vs nil in Q2.
Adj EBITDA rose 37.7% YoY to INR 7,420 Mn (-8.5% QoQ); OP margin stood at 18.65% (+216 bps YoY / -286 bps QoQ).
Calcination margins improved sequentially while Distillation eased on higher coal tar and energy costs; the CPC-GPC spread held steady QoQ and well above last year.
Some margin moderation is expected in Q4 as higher-cost GPC flows through.
valuation: Annual maintenance at the Indian calciner is complete (production restarted in Oct), the idle Lake Charles kiln is targeted to restart in Dec-26, and DGFT has allotted an initial GPC import quota of 598k MT (~85% of requirement), with the balance expected around Jan-27.

Net debt/EBITDA improves to 2.53x; refinancing window opens in Mar-27: Gross debt stood at USD 1,024 Mn and net debt at USD 851 Mn; net debt/adj EBITDA improved to 2.53x from 3.21x in Dec-25, below the ~3x medium-term target.
Valuation & Outlook: Q3CY26 marked a normalisation from Q2’s peak margins, though 9MCY26 adj EBITDA of INR 25.65 Bn (+51% YoY) is already ~80% of our CY26E EBITDA of INR 31,346 Mn.

Key update to maintain watch on Lake Charles kiln restart expected by Dec-26, working capital release, refinancing of the 12.25% USD 445 Mn notes from Mar-27 and CY26 FCF guidance of USD 60-65 Mn.
